tool.name: NormalisedKeyDiagnostics
tool.summary: Finds duplicate keys that only differ by spaces, case, Arabic-Indic digits, leading zeros, number-vs-text type or Arabic letter forms, and lists which raw values collapsed together. In JOIN mode it compares the keys of two tables and states, for each key that does not match exactly, after which normalisation steps it would match.

param.name: mode
param.dialogReference: DUPLICATES: find duplicate keys in one table. JOIN: diagnose the keys of the input against a join table.

param.name: in_table
param.dialogReference: Layer or table whose keys are checked (the left side in JOIN mode).

param.name: key_fields
param.dialogReference: One or more fields forming the key (a composite key when several).

param.name: join_table
param.dialogReference: JOIN mode: the layer or table to join to (the right side).

param.name: join_key_fields
param.dialogReference: JOIN mode: the key fields of the join table, in the same order and number as Key Fields.

param.name: normalisation
param.dialogReference: Normalisation steps to apply. Default: TRIM, CASE, DIGITS, LEADING_ZEROS, TYPE. ARABIC_LETTERS folds alef/yeh forms, tashkeel and tatweel; TA_MARBUTA also folds teh marbuta to heh.

param.name: write_groups
param.dialogReference: DUPLICATES mode: write DUP_GROUP (empty for unique keys and for keys with a null part; 0 instead when editing a shapefile or dBASE input in place) and DUP_COUNT fields, to a geodatabase copy (Output Features) or in place.

param.name: in_place
param.dialogReference: Write the group fields into the input itself (requires Write group fields). A backup copy is made first; unchecked by default.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: Copy of the input with DUP_GROUP and DUP_COUNT, when Write group fields is checked and Edit input in place is not. Must be in a geodatabase (a shapefile or dBASE copy is refused).

param.name: out_table
param.dialogReference: Detail table. DUPLICATES: DUP_GROUP, NORM_KEY, SRC_OID, RAW_KEY, DUP_COUNT for every row in a group. JOIN: LEFT_KEY, LEFT_COUNT, STATUS, RIGHT_KEY, RIGHT_COUNT, MATCH_AFTER per distinct key.

param.name: out_report
param.dialogReference: Optional Excel (.xlsx) or CSV report with Summary and Detail sheets.

param.name: issue_count
param.dialogReference: DUPLICATES: rows in duplicate groups. JOIN: keys that do not match exactly (derived).

tool.usage:
Normalisation steps always run in the fixed order TRIM, CASE, DIGITS, LEADING_ZEROS, TYPE, ARABIC_LETTERS, TA_MARBUTA, whatever order they are ticked in. Text keys are always put in Unicode canonical composition (NFC) before the steps and after each of them, so a decomposed spelling (as exported on macOS or copied from a PDF) is the same key as the precomposed one. A null in any key field never matches anything. With TRIM ticked the ends are stripped again after every later step, and LEADING_ZEROS also runs again after every later step. Selections and definition queries on input layers are honoured.

The input is never changed unless Write group fields and Edit input in place are both checked; then a backup copy is made first and all changes are written in one edit session. In-place editing is refused for layers with joined tables, a selection or a definition query. Without in-place editing, Write group fields writes a geodatabase copy of the input (Output Features) with DUP_GROUP and DUP_COUNT; a shapefile or dBASE copy is refused.

JOIN mode: MATCHED means identical characters, letter case included. Esri states that one-to-first joins are not case sensitive (one-to-many joins are), so a WOULD_MATCH whose MATCH_AFTER is only CASE may already join. MATCH_AFTER names the steps that were needed, not every step that changed a key. RIGHT_KEY is the right-hand key found at the earliest step in the fixed order; RIGHT_COUNT counts every right-hand row whose key equals the left key after all enabled steps.

Report: control characters show as <U+0001> in an Excel report and a lone surrogate as <U+D800> in both formats; the run warns when a report cell differs from the key, and the Output Table keeps the exact keys. Edge cases and limits are listed on the tool page (docs/tools/NormalisedKeyDiagnostics.md).
